evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Normally, it would take within the next five to ten minutes it would, would that be okay? — Rep says 5-10 minutes (script calls for 10-15), frames a quote outcome, but doesn't wait for a clear yes before moving into discovery.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today? — Asked early, before probing logistics.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'I just want to know an estimate and what is all allows be put on the truck.' Rep says 'Okay, no problem. We can walk you through how our pricing works...' and immediately pivots to logistics probing without following up on what 'what allows be put on the truck' really means to her.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Amy Smith), moving day (not explicitly stated but addresses given), city-to-city route (Tosin George, Texas to Georgetown, Texas), approx size (2000 sq ft stated, customer disputes to ~1400 sq ft actual) — all four topics touched, though size is contested.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: Rep correctly identifies 2000 sq ft (or larger), offers virtual walkthrough: 'So basically based on your home size normally we do a virtual offering that way we will just base it on the items that we are amazing. Do you have time to complete the virtual walk through today?' Customer declines live walkthrough, rep pivots to photos/videos option and sends a link. This is a proper walkthrough-routing call — the rep does not abandon or price aggressively when the customer resists, instead secures a commitment to submit photos for a more accurate assessment.
evidence_quotes.logistics_gathered: Property type (house), stories (one story first, two story second), bedrooms (3 and 4), parking access (driveway both locations, some narrowness noted), garage details (2-car, partially full). Missing: walking distance to truck, additional rooms beyond garage mentioned. Partial coverage of the seven-item list.
evidence_quotes.box_count: Yes, asked: 'And the typical backs count based on your home size. Upon checking here would be 115 to 135 box is. Do you feel that you fall within that range?' Customer says 150, then corrects to 'less than hundred.' Rep acknowledges update.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives a range for a typical 2000 sq ft home: 'a typical 2000 square foot home would normally take four movers and two trucks between six and a half to eight and a half hours to completely move. So, if they end up six and a half hours, that would be from 2600 and to eight and a half hours, which is up to $3,400.' However, this is anchored to disputed square footage; customer disputes the 2000 sq ft figure and the conversation devolves into a conflict over property size, not a personalized estimate. No pricing is finalized because the rep correctly routes to photos/video assessment instead.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses hourly rate ($100/hr per mover), truck/gas/insurance inclusions, two promises (damage coverage $2000, on-time guarantee with immediate discounting), and minimum/prorating structure (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments). This is comprehensive, but it happens mid-call before the actual routing, and the customer is confused ('I thought you said it start satisfied number' when she misunderstands 'hourly' for 'flat'). Framing is present but clarity breaks down under customer pushback.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_silence: Not asked. The call routes away from a final pricing agreement because the square footage is contested and the rep defers to photos/video assessment. No 'Does that feel fair?' checkpoint happens.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Delivered in full: 'Finally we have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage: Delivered in full: 'First is that we have no word damage coverage included on the R rate that you're paying us. We will provide up to $2,000 per move. That is to repair replace and reimburse for items.' (Phrasing is slightly garbled but the substance—$2K coverage, no deductible framing, built into rate—is complete.)
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No explicit 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent close. The two promises are explained but not confirmed as addressing the customer's concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'do you still have any other questions for any chance?' — this is a throwaway 'any questions' phrasing, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you?' version the rubric calls for.
evidence_quotes.catch_all: Not asked (e.g., 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?').
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Not asked. The call ends with 'Alright again. Thank you so much. Bye now.' and a link sent for photos. No 'Would you like our help with your move?' or commitment to book.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. Date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, and notes are not confirmed. The next step is photo/video submission via the link; no booking is attempted because the move is properly routed to a walkthrough assessment.

top_strength: Rep correctly identified the move as requiring a virtual walkthrough (large home, disputed square footage, complex item inventory) and pivoted smoothly to a photos/videos submission process instead of forcing an inaccurate quote — showing good judgment about limiting liability and ensuring accuracy.
coaching_note: In Section 2, when the customer said 'I just want to know an estimate and what is all allows be put on the truck,' the rep should have followed up ('Tell me more about what you mean by what can go on the truck — any items you're unsure about?') rather than pivoting straight to logistics probing; this missed the opportunity to surface restrictions/concerns early and would have strengthened the routing conversation.
